title: Inside the model: the core of LLMs

problems.title: Hallucination: the model doesn't know what it doesn't know
problems.why: Training rewards a confident answer, and the model has no reliable internal signal for "I am guessing".
problems.experiment: Take one domain (tax rules, drug doses). Build 500 questions with known answers. Measure how often each open model is confidently wrong, and test whether a cheap signal (asking 5 times and checking agreement, or reading internal activations) predicts those errors.
problems.reason: A domain test set with numbers is publishable and reusable.

problems.title: Reliable multi-step reasoning
problems.why: Small errors compound: 95% right per step is about 60% right over 10 steps. Models also give reasoning that doesn't match how they reached the answer.
problems.experiment: Measure how success drops with task length for 5 models on one task family (spreadsheet edits, multi-hop questions). Test one fix, such as checking each step with a second model.
problems.reason: The "error by length" curve is a known gap with few public measurements per domain.

problems.title: Thinking cost: models overthink easy questions
problems.why: Reasoning models spend thousands of hidden tokens on questions that need ten. Nobody has a reliable way to decide how much thinking a question needs.
problems.experiment: Route 1,000 questions to "think a little" or "think a lot" using a cheap classifier. Measure accuracy kept against tokens saved.
problems.reason: Cheap, measurable, and it saves money for every buyer.

problems.title: Continual learning: learn after deployment without forgetting
problems.why: Updating weights on new facts damages old skills ("catastrophic forgetting"). Today's fix is retraining from scratch or bolting on retrieval.
problems.experiment: Fine-tune a small model (1–3B) on a stream of weekly new facts. Measure how much old skill is lost per update, then compare 3 known methods (replay, LoRA adapters per period, model merging).
problems.reason: Small models make it feasible. A clean comparison is the goal, not beating labs.

problems.title: Using long context, not just fitting it
problems.why: Models accept a million tokens but miss facts in the middle and can't combine facts spread far apart.
problems.experiment: Build a test where the answer needs 3 facts from different parts of a 200-page document. Compare long context against retrieval against a memory agent.
problems.reason: Cheap, measurable, and directly useful to buyers.

problems.title: Personal memory across months of conversations
problems.why: What should an assistant remember, forget, update or never store? Memories go stale, contradict each other and leak private details.
problems.experiment: Build a 6-month synthetic user history with facts that change (moved city, new job). Measure how often 3 memory designs answer with the old fact.
problems.reason: Easy to measure, and every assistant product needs it.

problems.title: Understanding long video
problems.why: Models describe a short clip well but lose track of what happened across an hour of video: who did what, in which order.
problems.experiment: Ask 200 order-of-events questions about 30-minute public videos. Compare frame sampling against captions-then-text.
problems.reason: Video processing is costly, so keep the set small.

problems.title: Running out of human text; synthetic data collapse
problems.why: Good public text is nearly used up. Training on model-written text can narrow the model ("model collapse").
problems.experiment: Train small models over several generations on their own output, with and without filters. Measure diversity and accuracy loss per generation.
problems.reason: Small-scale results are interesting; large-scale claims need a lab.

problems.title: Evaluation itself is broken
problems.why: Benchmarks leak into training data and saturate within months. Scores stop telling you which model is better for your task.
problems.experiment: Write fresh questions after a model's cutoff date and compare its score on old against new questions in one area. The gap estimates contamination.
problems.reason: Cheap and needed by every buyer.

problems.title: World models and cause and effect
problems.why: Models learn patterns, not how the world works. They fail on "what would happen if" questions outside their training data.
problems.experiment: Build a small simulated world (a supply chain, a game) and test whether models predict what happens after an intervention they haven't seen.
problems.reason: The simulator becomes a reusable benchmark; links to AgentTwin.

problems.title: New architectures beyond the transformer
problems.why: Transformer cost grows with the square of context length. Alternatives (state-space models such as Mamba, hybrids) are cheaper but not yet clearly as good.
problems.experiment: Train tiny models of each type on the same data and compare quality per unit of compute on one long-sequence task.
problems.reason: Real answers need large training runs. Learn it at Explain depth.

problems.title: Learning from far less data
problems.why: A child learns language from about 100 million words; models need over 10 trillion. Nobody knows how to close most of that gap.
problems.experiment: The BabyLM challenge trains models on 100 million words or fewer. Enter it with one idea (curriculum order, a data quality filter).
problems.reason: BabyLM exists so that small teams can compete.

title: Safety and oversight: checking AI that may be smarter than you

problems.title: Scalable oversight: weaker people supervising stronger AI
problems.why: People can't check answers they don't understand, so training rewards what looks right.
problems.experiment: Have a small model judge a large model on questions with known answers. Plot how the judge's accuracy falls as the gap widens, then test whether debate or critiques help.
problems.reason: Open models of many sizes make the gap easy to vary.

problems.title: Control: staying safe even if the AI isn't trustworthy
problems.why: You need protection against a system that might work around you, not just one that makes honest mistakes.
problems.experiment: Build a trusted monitor: a small model watches a stronger agent's actions and blocks risky ones. Plant sabotage and measure the catch rate and the false alarms.
problems.reason: Mostly systems engineering, and a young field.

problems.title: Reward hacking: the model games the scorer
problems.why: Trained to pass tests, models learn to edit the tests, hard-code answers or claim success. The better the optimiser, the more it finds loopholes.
problems.experiment: Give coding agents tasks with weak tests and log how often they cheat (special-casing, deleting checks). Compare 3 ways of detecting it.
problems.reason: Easy to set up and a current lab worry.

problems.title: Prompt injection in tool-using agents
problems.why: The model can't reliably tell its instructions apart from text it reads in an email or web page. No defence holds against all attacks.
problems.experiment: Collect 300 injection attacks against an agent with email and file tools. Compare 5 defences on how many attacks get through and how much useful work is blocked.
problems.reason: Every company deploying agents has this problem now.

problems.title: Jailbreaks that keep working
problems.why: Every safety filter gets bypassed with new phrasing, other languages, role play or many examples in one prompt.
problems.experiment: Translate a public jailbreak set into 5 Indian languages and measure how much more often it gets through.
problems.reason: Low-resource languages are a known weak spot with few measurements.

problems.title: Detecting deception or "behaving only when watched"
problems.why: Lab studies have shown models acting differently when they believe they are being tested.
problems.experiment: Run the same tasks framed as a test and as real use, across open models. Measure the behaviour gap.
problems.reason: Careful design matters more than compute.

problems.title: Interpretability: reading what the model is thinking
problems.why: Billions of numbers with no labels, and concepts are smeared across many of them.
problems.experiment: Use TransformerLens and published sparse autoencoders on a small open model. Find where one concept lives and test whether switching it off changes the behaviour.
problems.reason: Many solo researchers publish here, though it takes maths patience.

problems.title: Unlearning: removing knowledge for good
problems.why: Removing a fact or skill usually hides it, and a little fine-tuning brings it back.
problems.experiment: Apply 3 unlearning methods to a small model, then try to recover the removed facts with 100 fine-tuning examples. Report what stays removed.
problems.reason: Cheap, matters to privacy law, and has a public benchmark (WMDP).

problems.title: Models memorising private training data
problems.why: Models can repeat phone numbers, keys or medical notes word for word. Training with privacy guarantees costs a lot of quality.
problems.experiment: Plant 100 fake secrets in fine-tuning data and measure how many can be pulled out, with and without privacy training.
problems.reason: Cheap, clear numbers, and regulated buyers care.

title: Edge AI and serving cost: AI on small devices and cheaper answers

problems.title: Shrinking models below 4 bits without losing quality
problems.why: At 2 bits or "ternary" weights (−1, 0, +1), quality usually drops sharply, especially for reasoning and non-English text.
problems.experiment: Quantize 3 open models to 4, 3 and 2 bits with 3 methods. Measure the quality loss per task type.
problems.reason: Runs on one GPU and fills a measurement gap.

problems.title: The memory cost of long conversations (the KV cache)
problems.why: Every token of context is kept in GPU memory while answering, so long chats and many users run out of memory before compute.
problems.experiment: Compare 3 cache-compression methods on one open model at 32k context. Measure memory saved against accuracy lost.
problems.reason: Single-GPU experiment with a direct cost story.

problems.title: Always-on sensing on tiny chips (TinyML)
problems.why: Microcontrollers have kilobytes of memory and run on coin batteries. Useful models must be thousands of times smaller.
problems.experiment: Train a sound or vibration detector (machine fault, cough) that fits under 256 KB and runs on a ₹500 board. Measure accuracy and battery life.
problems.reason: Cheap hardware and a demo anyone understands.

problems.title: Learning on the device while keeping data private
problems.why: Federated learning (training across many phones without collecting their data) struggles with very different users, unreliable devices and attacks.
problems.experiment: Simulate 1,000 phones with uneven data and compare 3 methods on accuracy and privacy leakage.
problems.reason: Simulation is cheap; real fleets need a partner.

problems.title: Energy per answer
problems.why: AI's electricity demand is growing faster than grids, and few people measure the cost of a token end to end.
problems.experiment: Measure watt-hours per answer for one model across settings (batch size, quantization, cache reuse) on one GPU and one laptop. Publish a cost and energy table.
problems.reason: A clear number that every buyer of AI cares about.

problems.title: Trusting a model running on someone else's device
problems.why: How do you prove a device runs the approved, untampered model and that its answers weren't changed?
problems.experiment: Build a demo that signs each answer with the model's fingerprint and test which tampering it catches.
problems.reason: A narrow proof of concept; full solutions need hardware support.

problems.title: Robot hands that cope with new objects
problems.why: Folding laundry or handling soft and unfamiliar things fails outside the lab. Touch sensing and fine control are weak.
problems.experiment: Not a solo build. Watch the open robot models (such as Physical Intelligence's π0 family).
problems.reason: It needs hardware and large data.

problems.title: Too little robot training data
problems.why: The web has trillions of words but very few recorded robot actions, and every lab uses its own format.
problems.experiment: Build a checker that scores public robot datasets on quality (missing frames, mislabelled actions, sensor drift) and publish the results.
problems.reason: A data quality problem, which one careful person can measure.

problems.title: The gap between simulation and reality
problems.why: Robots trained in simulation fail on real friction, light and wear.
problems.experiment: In a free simulator (MuJoCo, Isaac Sim), measure how a trained policy degrades as you randomise physics.
problems.reason: Simulation-only results are a partial answer.

problems.title: Proving an autonomous system is safe
problems.why: Driving enough miles to prove safety is impossible, so you need scenario testing, and nobody agrees which scenarios are enough.
problems.experiment: Generate scenarios for one narrow case (a warehouse robot crossing), run them in simulation, and measure how many rare failures random tests find against targeted tests.
problems.reason: The same "faced world" idea as AgentTwin, applied to machines.

problems.title: Flying and moving without GPS
problems.why: Drones and robots lose position indoors, underground or when GPS is jammed, and drift builds up within minutes.
problems.experiment: On a public drone flight dataset, compare 3 open visual positioning methods on drift per minute.
problems.reason: Public datasets exist; real flights need hardware.

problems.title: Batteries limit every robot
problems.why: Humanoids and drones run 1–2 hours. Energy density improves only a few percent a year.
problems.experiment: No solo build. Track how battery energy per kilogram improves each year.
problems.reason: It is a chemistry and manufacturing problem.

problems.title: Estimating query sizes (the 40-year database problem)
problems.why: Query planners guess how many rows each step returns. Guesses can be off by 1,000 times and pick slow plans; learned estimators haven't replaced the old ones.
problems.experiment: On the public JOB benchmark, compare the default planner's guesses with a small learned model. Measure the time lost to bad guesses.
problems.reason: Well studied, so a gain must be clean and real.

problems.title: Keeping thousands of GPUs busy
problems.why: Large training runs lose a lot of time to failures, slow machines and waiting on the network. A single bad GPU can stall a whole run.
problems.experiment: Simulate a 1,000-GPU job with realistic failure rates and compare checkpoint strategies on time lost.
problems.reason: Simulation is solo-friendly; real proof needs a cluster.

problems.title: Proving AI-written code is correct
problems.why: AI writes code faster than people can review it. Tests catch some bugs; proof tools (Lean, Dafny) are hard to use.
problems.experiment: Have an LLM write small functions plus a formal proof in Dafny. Measure how often the proof passes and the code is truly right.
problems.reason: Free tools, and results are pass or fail.

problems.title: Same input, different LLM answer
problems.why: Even at "temperature 0", batching and GPU maths make answers vary between runs, which breaks audits and repeatable tests.
problems.experiment: Measure how often answers change across runs and providers for 1,000 prompts. Test which serving settings make them repeatable.
problems.reason: Cheap, and regulated buyers need it.

problems.title: Retrieval that finds the right passage
problems.why: Most wrong RAG answers come from fetching the wrong text. Search quality drops on tables, numbers, acronyms and mixed languages.
problems.experiment: Build 300 questions over messy enterprise-style documents and compare 4 retrieval setups on whether the right passage is in the top 5.
problems.reason: Measurable and directly useful.

problems.title: Matching records that refer to the same thing
problems.why: The same customer, drug or company is spelled differently across systems ("entity resolution"), and it still needs people to check at scale.
problems.experiment: On a public benchmark, compare a rules approach, an embedding approach and an LLM judge on accuracy and cost per million pairs.
problems.reason: Your home ground, and the cost numbers are new.

problems.title: Useful analytics with privacy guarantees
problems.why: Differential privacy (adding maths noise so no person can be identified) makes small groups' numbers useless.
problems.experiment: Apply it to a public census-style table and measure which questions stay accurate enough to act on.
problems.reason: Clear numbers; the buyers are governments and health bodies.

problems.title: Data meaning, not just data movement
problems.why: Pipelines move data correctly, yet "revenue" means three different things in three tables, and nothing checks the meaning.
problems.experiment: Build a checker that compares metric definitions across dbt models and dashboards, and flags conflicts on an open project.
problems.reason: Useful, but harder to state as one number.

problems.title: The memory wall
problems.why: Chips compute far faster than memory can feed them. Serving LLMs is mostly waiting for memory, not maths.
problems.experiment: Profile one open model on one GPU and show what share of time is memory-bound at different batch sizes.
problems.reason: A good learning project and an explainer, not a breakthrough.

problems.title: Connecting thousands of chips
problems.why: Big models span many chips, and moving data between them costs time and power. Optical links and new network designs are still being proven.
problems.experiment: No solo build. Learn how NVLink, InfiniBand and optical links compare.
problems.reason: Needs hardware labs.

problems.title: Power and cooling for AI data centres
problems.why: Racks now draw over 100 kW, and grids and cooling can't keep up. New sites wait years for power.
problems.experiment: Model the power, water and cost of a 10 MW AI data centre in 3 Indian cities from public data.
problems.reason: A strong explainer built from public data.

problems.title: AI for chip design
problems.why: Placing and routing billions of transistors takes months of expert work. Published AI results are disputed.
problems.experiment: On the open OpenROAD flow, compare a learned placement method with the default on one open chip design.
problems.reason: Free tools exist, but gains are hard to prove.

problems.title: Computing with light or analog circuits
problems.why: Photonic and analog chips promise far lower energy, but noise and precision limit them.
problems.experiment: No solo build. Track the lab results and the first products.
problems.reason: Needs fabrication.

problems.title: Quantum error correction
problems.why: Qubits make errors constantly. A useful quantum computer needs thousands of error-corrected qubits; today's machines have a handful of logical ones.
problems.experiment: No solo build. Read one review a quarter.
problems.reason: Needs quantum hardware and a deep physics background.

problems.title: Memory-unsafe code everywhere
problems.why: Most serious security bugs in C and C++ come from memory errors. Rewriting billions of lines in Rust by hand is unaffordable.
problems.experiment: Have an LLM translate 50 small C programs to safe Rust and measure how many compile, pass tests and avoid "unsafe" blocks.
problems.reason: Pass-or-fail results and a public push for memory safety.

problems.title: Malicious packages in software supply chains
problems.why: Attackers publish look-alike packages and hijack maintainers. Thousands of packages ship daily, and review can't keep up.
problems.experiment: Train a detector on known malicious npm or PyPI packages and test it on a month of new uploads.
problems.reason: Public data and a clear catch rate.

problems.title: AI that finds vulnerabilities before attackers do
problems.why: Fuzzing finds crashes but not logic bugs. AI helps, but false alarms waste defenders' time.
problems.experiment: Run an LLM bug-finder against 20 projects with known past vulnerabilities and measure what it finds against false alarms.
problems.reason: Measurable, and in demand from defenders.

problems.title: Post-quantum migration
problems.why: Future quantum computers will break today's encryption, and organisations don't know where they use vulnerable crypto.
problems.experiment: Build a scanner that finds vulnerable crypto use in code and configs, and test it on 50 open-source projects.
problems.reason: Governments have set migration deadlines.

problems.title: Identity when voices and faces can be faked
problems.why: Video-call and voice-clone fraud beats "I recognise them" checks, and passwords still get phished.
problems.experiment: Design a call-back and passkey check for one payment approval flow and measure how many staged deepfake attempts it stops.
problems.reason: Useful, but staged tests are small.

problems.title: Turning maths into machine-checked proofs
problems.why: Translating written maths into a proof language (Lean) is slow, so few results are checked by machine.
problems.experiment: Have an LLM translate 100 textbook proofs (Class 11 and 12 level) into Lean. Measure how many check, and publish the set.
problems.reason: Free tools, pass-or-fail results and an active community.

problems.title: Weather beyond two weeks
problems.why: AI weather models now beat physics models for days ahead, but skill fades after about 2 weeks, and seasonal forecasts stay weak.
problems.experiment: Compare open AI forecasts with simple climatology at 1, 2 and 4 weeks ahead for one region.
problems.reason: Open data; making a real gain is hard.

problems.title: Predicting what a protein does or binds to
problems.why: Structure prediction (AlphaFold) is largely solved; function, binding and design that works in a lab are not.
problems.experiment: Use open protein models (ESM) to rank variants on the public ProteinGym benchmark and test one new idea.
problems.reason: Fine on public benchmarks; lab proof needs partners.

problems.title: Predicting drug toxicity early
problems.why: Most drug candidates fail late because of side effects that early tests miss.
problems.experiment: On public toxicity datasets (Tox21), test whether adding LLM-read literature features improves prediction.
problems.reason: Public benchmarks exist, and the bar is high.

problems.title: Finding new battery and material candidates
problems.why: Millions of possible materials, slow lab tests, and models that predict properties but not whether something can be made.
problems.experiment: Use the Materials Project database to screen candidates for one property.
problems.reason: Real progress needs a lab. Explain depth.

problems.title: Deep theory: P vs NP, the Riemann hypothesis, unifying physics
problems.why: Open for decades. Progress needs new mathematics, not more computing.
problems.experiment: None solo for now. Enjoy them at Explain depth.
problems.reason: Follow for curiosity.

problems.title: Ageing and fusion
problems.why: Each needs labs or reactors and decades of work.
problems.experiment: None solo. Read one good review a quarter to keep up.
problems.reason: Follow.

problems.title: Spotting deepfakes
problems.why: Detectors break with every new generator.
problems.experiment: Train a detector on images from older generators and measure how it fails on the newest ones. The size of that drop is the finding.
problems.reason: A public benchmark and a clear number.

problems.title: Proving where content came from
problems.why: Watermarks are stripped by editing, and signed content (C2PA) is rarely used end to end.
problems.experiment: Test how many common edits (crop, re-encode, screenshot) remove each watermark method.
problems.reason: Easy to measure, though the real fix is adoption.

problems.title: An AI tutor that measurably raises learning
problems.why: Many tutors feel helpful, but few show test-score gains in controlled trials, and some make students lean on them.
problems.experiment: Run a 6-week trial with 2 groups of students on one topic, comparing a hints-only tutor with one that gives answers. Measure scores before and after.
problems.reason: Needs willing students and careful design.

problems.title: Fact-checking at the speed of rumour
problems.why: False claims spread in minutes; checks take hours or days.
problems.experiment: Build a pipeline that matches new claims to existing fact-checks, and measure how many are caught within an hour.
problems.reason: Measurable, and the hard part is distribution.

title: India: hard problems at India's scale

problems.title: AI in Indian languages costs more and works worse
problems.why: Tokenizers split Indian scripts into many more pieces than English, so the same sentence costs about 3 to 8 times more and quality drops. Clean training data is scarce, especially Hinglish.
problems.experiment: Measure the "token tax" and accuracy gap across 10 Indian languages for 8 models. Build a small, clean Hinglish dataset and show what it does to a small model.
problems.reason: Few measure it carefully, and the IndiaAI Mission and funders care.

problems.title: Speech recognition for dialects and code-mixed talk
problems.why: Models trained on standard Hindi fail on Bhojpuri, Marwari, Hinglish switching mid-sentence, and noisy streets and phone lines.
problems.experiment: Record or collect 500 clips across 5 dialects. Measure the word error rate of open models (Whisper, AI4Bharat's models) and test a small fine-tune.
problems.reason: Open models exist and the error rate is a clear number.

problems.title: Reading Indian documents: land records, forms, handwriting
problems.why: Scanned land records and government forms mix scripts, stamps and handwriting. Text recognition for Indian scripts is far behind English.
problems.experiment: Measure text recognition accuracy on 300 public scanned records in 3 scripts across 4 tools, then extract key fields (owner, area, survey number).
problems.reason: Public scans exist, and the field-level accuracy number matters to banks and courts.

problems.title: Useful AI on a ₹10,000 phone, offline
problems.why: Memory, battery and heat limits. Most "on-device" demos run on flagship phones, while most Indian phones are budget models.
problems.experiment: Run a 1–3B model offline on a budget Android phone for one task (form filling in Hindi). Measure speed, battery used per answer and accuracy.
problems.reason: Easy to demo, and the audience is hundreds of millions of phones.

problems.title: Addresses that machines can't read
problems.why: Indian addresses are free text ("behind the temple, near the old well"). Deliveries, ambulances and KYC fail on them. DIGIPIN, a national digital address code, is new.
problems.experiment: Parse and geocode 5,000 public-style addresses with 3 methods and measure how many land within 100 metres.
problems.reason: Clear numbers, and logistics and fintech care.

problems.title: Voice-clone and UPI scams in Indian languages
problems.why: Scam calls and messages now use cloned voices in Indian languages. Detectors and scam filters are mostly trained on English.
problems.experiment: Build a test set of real and cloned voices, plus scam and genuine SMS, in Hindi and 2 other languages. Measure how open detectors hold up.
problems.reason: A clear gap and a clear number.

problems.title: Hyperlocal monsoon and flood forecasts
problems.why: Global AI weather models are good at large scale, but rain for one district a few hours ahead is still poor, and floods in Assam and Kerala hit with little warning.
problems.experiment: Take open forecasts (GraphCast, or ERA5 data) and IMD station data. Measure the error for 10 districts, then fine-tune a small local rain correction.
problems.reason: Open data and a clear error number, and farmers, insurers and cities care.

problems.title: Crop yield and stress for small farms
problems.why: Satellite pixels (10 metres) are bigger than many Indian plots, and ground truth is scarce.
problems.experiment: Use free Sentinel-2 images for one district with published yield data. Compare yield prediction from pixels against plot boundaries.
problems.reason: Ground truth is the hard part, so pick a district with good records.

problems.title: Groundwater running out
problems.why: Much of north-west India pumps more than rain refills. Wells are measured only a few times a year.
problems.experiment: Combine public well readings with satellite gravity data (GRACE) and forecast levels for one district a year ahead.
problems.reason: Public data; validation is slow.

problems.title: Where Delhi's air pollution comes from
problems.why: Stubble burning, traffic, industry, dust and weather mix differently every day, and sources are argued over every winter.
problems.experiment: Join public pollution sensor data with satellite fire counts and wind. Estimate the daily share from crop fires for one season.
problems.reason: Open data, high public interest and a clear number.

problems.title: Grid forecasting with lots of solar
problems.why: Solar and wind swing with the weather, and electricity distributors lose money balancing it.
problems.experiment: Forecast next-day solar output for one state from open weather and generation data and compare it with a simple baseline.
problems.reason: Public data in places; the buyers are utilities (a sales cycle).

problems.title: Too few doctors in rural clinics
problems.why: Primary health centres often have one doctor or none. Triage tools must work with little data, in local languages, and be safe.
problems.experiment: Build a symptom triage test from public clinical vignettes in Hindi and measure how often open models choose the safe referral.
problems.reason: Measurable in simulation; real use needs medical partners.

problems.title: Court case backlog
problems.why: India has about 50 million pending cases. Delays come from scheduling, missing papers and adjournments.
problems.experiment: From public eCourts data for one district, predict which cases are likely to be adjourned and measure how well that works.
problems.reason: Public but messy data, and the buyer is government.

problems.title: Credit for people with no credit history
problems.why: Millions have no credit record. Models using other data can be unfair and hard to explain to a regulator.
problems.experiment: On a public lending dataset, compare accuracy against fairness gaps for 3 models, plus the explanation each gives a rejected applicant.
problems.reason: Measurable, and lenders and regulators care.

problems.title: Matching informal workers to jobs
problems.why: Most Indian workers are informal, have no CV and find work by word of mouth.
problems.experiment: Build a voice-first profile in Hindi (skills, location, availability) and measure matching accuracy against 200 real-style job posts.
problems.reason: The tech is testable; reaching workers is the hard part.

problems.title: Driving in Indian traffic
problems.why: No lanes, mixed vehicles (cows, autos, carts), and rules followed loosely. Self-driving models trained in the US or China fail here.
problems.experiment: On the public India Driving Dataset (IDD), measure how much a detector trained on Western data drops in accuracy, and how much fine-tuning recovers.
problems.reason: Public data; full autonomy is a lab-scale problem.
